scenes.headline: How GLM 5.2 makes a million-token context affordable
scenes.sub: Z.ai's open mixture of experts, sparse attention, and the IndexShare trick.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Misty! GLM 5.2 reads a million tokens at once. Here's the trick that makes that affordable.

scenes.text: Neighbouring sparse-attention layers pick almost the same tokens, so GLM 5.2 runs its indexer once per four layers and reuses the choice.
scenes.say: The idea: neighbouring layers pick almost the same tokens to attend to. So compute that choice once per four layers, and reuse it.

steps.say: GLM 5.2 is a mixture of experts: seven hundred forty-four billion parameters, forty billion active per token.
Its attention is sparse. A lightweight indexer picks the top k tokens worth attending to, instead of the whole sequence.
On top, a multi-token prediction layer drafts ahead, now accepting about twenty percent more tokens per check.

scenes.title: IndexShare: one indexer per four layers

steps.label: Adjacent layers pick 70-100% of the same tokens
steps.say: At a million tokens, running that indexer in every layer dominates the cost. And neighbouring layers pick almost the same tokens anyway.

steps.label: Index once, reuse it in the next 3 layers
steps.say: So GLM 5.2 computes the index once per four layers, and the next three reuse it.

scenes.label: lower per-token FLOPs at a 1M-token context, quality essentially intact
scenes.note: share across 8 layers instead, and long context starts to degrade
scenes.say: Reported: two point nine times fewer FLOPs per token at a million tokens. Share across eight layers, and fidelity slips.

items.say: Pretraining ran to twenty-eight and a half trillion tokens.
Post-training moved to critic-based PPO, with token-level advantages from single rollouts.
So a run thousands of tool calls long is compacted, not capped.
A hack filter blocks suspect calls and returns dummy information, so the rollout continues.

scenes.title: FrontierSWE, long-horizon coding
scenes.say: On long-horizon coding it nearly catches Claude Opus. On harder standard benchmarks, the closed frontier still leads.

scenes.text: Reuse what's nearly identical instead of recomputing it: that turns a million-token context into something you can serve.

recap: Sparse attention picks the top-k tokens
One indexer serves every four layers
Critic-based PPO for very long runs
scenes.say: To recap: sparse attention, an indexer shared across four layers, and training built for very long runs.
